# A global cubic barrier for arbitrary unique-corner losses

This theorem uses the stronger cubic triangle inequality and has NO cap
ceiling, profile, small-loss, or initial equality hypothesis. It is an
ordinary planar result and does not assert compatibility with neighboring
mixed fibers.

## 1. Raw functional and exact loss derivatives

For positive data k,Q_i,sigma_i, i=1,2,3, define

    M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i,
    f_i=2sqrt(k Q_i)/(sigma_i M),
    P=f_1f_2f_3,
    Psi=f_1^2+f_2^2+f_3^2+P.

Its logarithmic derivative weights are

    E_i=f_i partial_(f_i)Psi=2f_i^2+P,
    C=sum_i E_i=2sum_i f_i^2+3P.

Under a unit loss of total area k and the same loss of cap area Q_s,
with other caps and all three sections fixed, the derivative is -alpha_s,
where

    alpha_s=C/(2k)+E_s/(2Q_s)-C/(M sigma_s).

Indeed d log f_i=(dk)/(2k)+(dQ_i)/(2Q_i)-dM/M when sections are fixed,
and dM=-1/sigma_s in this loss direction. Setting T_s=1/sqrt(Q_s/k) gives

    2k alpha_s=C+E_s T_s^2-C f_s T_s.                 (1)

## 2. Every unique loss is strictly inward at the cubic boundary

Suppose Psi=4 at positive data. Then

    C=8+P,
    0<f_s<2,
    4E_s-C f_s^2=P(4-f_s^2)>0.                       (2)

The middle strict bound follows immediately from positivity of all terms
in Psi. Minimizing the quadratic (1) over all real T_s yields

    2k alpha_s
       >=C-C^2 f_s^2/(4E_s)
        =C P(4-f_s^2)/(4E_s)>0.                      (3)

Thus EVERY unique-cap loss has a strictly negative derivative at every
positive cubic boundary point. The proof does not require the other row
inequalities, a cap ceiling, a cap floor, a profile, or geometric
realizability of that boundary data.

## 3. Finite simultaneous loss theorem

Take any E_1,E_2,E_3>=0, E=sum E_i, and the path

    k(t)=k_0-tE,
    Q_i(t)=Q_i0-tE_i,
    sigma_i(t)=sigma_i0,       0<=t<=1.                (4)

Assume all final data remain positive. If initially Psi<=4, then finally
Psi<=4, with strict inequality whenever E>0.

Proof: the path stays in the positive orthant and the functional is smooth.
At every time when Psi=4 its derivative is -sum_i E_i alpha_i<0 if E>0,
by (3). An initially tight value therefore immediately enters Psi<4.
If the path ever reaches 4 again, take its first contact from below;
its left derivative there would be nonnegative, contradicting the strict
negative derivative. The same reasoning excludes a first contact at the
final endpoint. If E=0, all data are unchanged. This proves the finite
claim without an unproved compactness or flow assertion.

## 4. Actual bodies inside a triangle with all three chords fixed

Let T be a triangle with an interior source and three balanced spanning
normals whose caps strictly isolate its three distinct vertices. Let C_T
be the convex hull of the six actual cutting-ray endpoints. For ANY convex
body K satisfying

    C_T subset K subset T,

the three full source sections are unchanged. The removed region is
partitioned, up to null boundaries, among the three unique vertex-corner
triangles. If E_i is the removed area in corner i, the raw data of T and K
are exactly the endpoints (4). All cap and total areas remain positive
because K contains the full-dimensional six-ray core and the source lies
in its interior.

The independently proved triangle identity

    4-Psi(T)=4(sqrt(prod u_i)-sqrt(prod(1-u_i)))^2>=0

appears in `candidate d61c49578c90db6d`.
Applying Section 3 gives

    Psi(K)<=4,

strictly unless K=T. Equality of area with a closed convex subset forces
equality of the bodies: any omitted point admits a strict separating cap
of positive triangle area. Thus the strictness statement is geometric.

Finally Psi<=4 implies every individual Lorentz row:

    f_i+(f_j+f_l)^2/4<=2.

Indeed, as all f_i<2,

    Psi=f_i^2+(f_j+f_l)^2-(2-f_i)f_j f_l
        >=f_i^2+(2+f_i)(f_j+f_l)^2/4.

If Psi<4, every such row is strict. Therefore every proper core-containing
convex inner body of T satisfies all three rows strictly, with arbitrary
corner-loss size and arbitrary boundary regularity. This includes the
actual cap-band quadrilateral examples whose containing triangle leaves
the cap band.

The argument also extends to weak distinct-vertex incidences when an actual
containing triangle is approximated through strict incidences and its exact
loss data stay positive; no such limiting extension is needed for the
strict-incidence theorem above.

## Scope

This removes the initial-cap-ceiling obstruction for actual unique-corner
truncations with unchanged sections. It does not control a double-sector
gain, changing section lengths, or an arbitrary quadrilateral lacking this
containing-triangle structure. Those cases remain separate from the proved
global loss barrier.
